newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Doctors say maternal mortality can be addressed.
newsitem.headline: Doctors say maternal mortality can be addressed.

text.p: The president of an international group of physicians on Monday accused people of ignoring the problem of women who die giving birth and said this could be reversed with the minimum of material changes.

"Since the beginning of the 1990s, six million women have died in childbirth...It did not attract world attention because of a conspiracy of silence," said Dr Daniel Weinstein, president of the World Society on Labour and Delivery.
"The reason is simple...It is an embarrassing issue which nobody wants to deal with," he said.

His speech was given at the start of a week-long conference, the first of its kind, grouping more than 750 doctors and other medical specialists to discuss maternal mortality and how it could be reduced.
The United Nations Children's Fund estimated that in 1990, 600,000 women died in childbirth, mainly in developing countries. But Weinstein's group says the figure is closer to one million annually.

"We estimate at 45 million the number of women who are handicapped every year after childbirth complications. And more than 8.2 million infants die after delivery due to lack of medical care," Weinstein told the meeting.
He said the meeting aimed to develop a plan to send a team of specialists to an African or Asian country with a high rate of childbirth deaths to help improve conditions.
"We should show the world that with adequate minimum material conditions, developing countries can reduce dramatically the maternal mortality tragedy," he said.
